newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-FIORENTINA FACE DIFFICULT GAME AGAINST JUVENTUS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FIORENTINA FACE DIFFICULT GAME AGAINST JUVENTUS.

text.p: Fiorentina coach Claudio Ranieri is apprehensive about Sunday's league clash with serie A leaders Juventus.
The home game comes at a delicate moment for Fiorentina, who were surprisingly beaten 2-1 by third-from-bottom Verona last Sunday and are now in 11th place, 13 points behind runaway leaders Juventus.
"This is my most difficult game since I've been at Fiorentina. We're at a turning point, it's now or never", says Ranieri, who has found himself under pressure from disgruntled fans.

Traditionally bitter rivalry between Juventus and Fiorentina has in the past led to litigation between prominent Fiorentina fans such as film director Franco Zefferelli and former Juventus president Giampiero Boniperti.

Ranieri seems likely to opt for a 4-4-2 formation with Russian and ex-Everton winger Andreij Kanchelskis partnering Fiorentina captain Gabriel Batistuta of Argentina in attack and with Swede Stefan Schwarz, Portugal's Rui Costa, Sandro Cois and Giovanni Piacentini in midfield.
Juventus travel south with an almost full-strength squad, missing only two long-term injury victims -- Croat striker Alen Boksic and midfielder Antonio Conte.
Influential Juventus central defender Paolo Montero of Uruguay will renew Latin American rivalry with Batistuta.

"Batistuta is one of the best strikers in the world and I like his style -- he's fearless, powerful and sets his sails straight for goal, a real team leader," said Montero. "This'll be a very special game, hotter than usual because of their defeat by Verona."
Alessandro Del Piero and Michele Padovano lead the Juventus attack in a match which follows 1-0 Juventus wins in Turin last September and in Florence in March of last season.
